title: "11. Remote computing"
---

```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(dMod2)
# the local job runs in an empty folder, where it finds no shared objects of other articles
.work <- tempfile("remote-computing-")
dir.create(.work)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = .work)
.outdir <- options(dMod2.outdir = NULL)
```

dMod2 parallelizes along two axes: conditions of one objective evaluation in threads, independent
fits and profiles in processes. `distributedComputing()` runs any R code as tasks in processes
detached from the session, locally, over ssh or as a SLURM array job. The local job below runs at
page build; commands for other machines are shown, not run.

## Threads and processes

`options(dMod2.cores = n)`, or `obj(pars, cores = n)` for one call, solves the conditions of an
evaluation in `n` threads of an OpenMP team inside cppDE, constant in size within a session. The
guide model has two conditions, so this axis uses at most two threads; many conditions, or `em()`
with many groups, gain in proportion. A single condition never uses it. Predictions do not pass
through forked processes: sending back the arrays of states and sensitivities costs more than
computing them.

`mstrust()`, `msem()` and `profile()` run independent fits as processes through `cores`. With one
number, fits are forks of the session, each solving conditions in one thread: a forked child never
starts the thread team, and BLAS and OpenMP stay at one thread across the fork.
`cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2)` runs four fits with two threads each in fresh R processes (a
PSOCK cluster), as always on Windows. Each process holds a copy of the predictions, so memory
grows with the process count; keep the product of both below the core count.

| where | argument | axis |
|---|---|---|
| one evaluation | `options(dMod2.cores = )`, `obj(pars, cores = )` | conditions, threads |
| `em()` | `cores` | groups and conditions, threads |
| `mstrust()`, `msem()` | `cores`, `c(fits = , conditions = )` | fits, processes |
| `profile()` | `cores`, `c(pars = , conditions = )` | parameters, processes |
| `distributedComputing()` | `tasks`, `on` | tasks, detached processes |

```{r}
options(dMod2.cores = 2)
fits <- mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 20,
                cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2))
profiles <- profile(obj, best, names(best), fixed = gauge, cores = 8)
```

## Tasks and job code

`distributedComputing(expr, tasks, on)` evaluates `expr` once per task in a fresh R process; the
value is the task result. `tasks` is a count, a list or vector with one element per task, or a
data frame with one row per task. Inside `expr`:

- `task`: the element or row (as a list, `task$n`), `NULL` when `tasks` is a count,
- `taskId`: the position in `tasks`,
- `cores`: cores available to the task, e.g. for `mstrust(cores = cores)`,
  `parallel::mclapply(mc.cores = cores)` or `options(dMod2.cores = cores)`,
- `jobname`: the job name.

`input` names the session objects the code reads, functions included, by default all objects of
the calling environment. The process attaches dMod2 and the R defaults; other packages are loaded
by the code, and session options such as `dMod2.cores` do not reach it.

Example: coverage of the 95% t interval for the mean of exponential samples, one task per sample
size, on the local machine:

```{r coverage, eval = TRUE}
interval <- function(y) t.test(y)$conf.int
sizes <- data.frame(n = c(5, 10, 20, 50))
job <- distributedComputing(
  {
    message("task ", taskId, ": samples of size ", task$n)
    covered <- replicate(2000, {
      ci <- interval(rexp(task$n))
      ci[1] < 1 && 1 < ci[2]
    })
    data.frame(n = task$n, coverage = mean(covered))
  },
  tasks = sizes, on = localNode(cores = 1), jobname = "coverage", input = "interval", seed = 1
)
job
```

The call returns once tasks have started. `job` is a list of functions: `check()` reports task
states, `wait()` polls until none runs, `get()` joins the results, here into one data frame.

```{r follow, eval = TRUE}
job$check()
job$wait(interval = 1)
job$get()
```

Task `i` uses seed `seed + i`, independent of worker and order; without `seed` one is drawn. A
task that errors returns the `try-error`, the others go on.

## Job folder layout

At submission the job files go into a temporary stage, copied to every node as one `tar` stream
over ssh into `<jobname>_folder/<k>` of the home directory, `k` the node number. On `"localhost"`
the folder is in the working directory and no ssh is used. The local `<jobname>_folder` also holds
the manifest `job.rds`. After the local job:

```{r folder, eval = TRUE}
list.files("coverage_folder", recursive = TRUE)
```

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `workspace.RData` | objects of `input`; `zstd`-compressed when available locally |
| `tasks.rds` | tasks as a list, one entry per data frame row |
| `job.R` | R script of a task |
| model files | sources, objects or shared objects, see [Model files and builds](#model-files-and-builds) |
| `build.sh`, `files.txt`, `build.log` | model build on the node, build output |
| `slot_<k>.sh`, `.pid`, `.run` | runner script of node `k`, process ID of the script and of the running task |
| `job.sh`, `env.sh` | SLURM only: job script from the template, job environment |
| `task_<i>.out`, `task_<i>.rds` | output and result of task `i` |

`job.R` is the same for every task, called as `Rscript job.R <taskId> <cores>` with output in
`task_<taskId>.out`:

```{r jobscript, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines("coverage_folder/1/job.R"))
```

It attaches dMod2, loads workspace and shared objects, reads the task, sets the seed and evaluates
the code in `try()`, writing `task_<taskId>.rds` for `get()`. Tasks share nothing but files. The
code runs in the job folder of the node; files written there come back with `get(all = TRUE)`.

## Nodes and workers

`on` says where tasks run:

```{r}
on <- localNode()                                        # the local machine, with the free cores
on <- localNode(cores = 8)
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"))                  # each node with the free cores there
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 10)
on <- sshNodes(cores = c(server1 = 24, server2 = 20))
on <- sshNodes(c("localhost", "server1"))                # the local machine and one more
on <- slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 8, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

A node is an ssh destination (`"host"`, `"user@host"`) with key authentication, since no terminal
takes a password. `"localhost"` runs without ssh, in the session shell and working directory, with
the R and library paths of the session, so no second dMod2 install is needed;
`localNode()` is `sshNodes("localhost")`.

Each node is one worker. Task `i` goes to worker `(i - 1) %% W + 1` of `W`; a worker runs the assigned tasks
in sequence, each with the `cores` of the node. `tasks = NULL`, the default, gives one task per
worker.

`cores` per task is one number, a vector named by node, or `NULL` for the free cores at
submission. `detectFreeCores()` counts cores minus the one-minute load average, on a local
Windows machine minus the processor load since the previous call, at least 1, locally or over ssh; a node gets at most the free cores, with a warning if given more.

```{r}
detectFreeCores(c("localhost", "server1", "server2"))
```

On each node `slot_<k>.sh` calls `Rscript job.R` for each task of the node in turn, started as
`nohup setsid sh slot_<k>.sh &`, so it survives the end of the ssh connection or the session.
Tasks run with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`, so BLAS and OpenMP start only threads
the code asks for, and with `libs` first in the library paths.

## Model files and builds

The model files of a job are those of the model objects in `input` (`obsfn`, `parfn`, `prdfn`,
objectives), found through their sources; without any, all model files of
`getOption("dMod2.outdir")`, else of the working directory. `build` sets how they reach the nodes:

- `"compile"`: sources are copied and `build.sh` compiles them into one shared object against the
  cppDE installed on the node, with cppDE headers, SUNDIALS, KLU, the model `-D` switches and
  `-O2`. `buildCores` compilers run at once, by default the node cores, at most 16. Past the
  command-line limit objects go through a static archive, `buildBundle` sources per translation
  unit.
- `"link"`: object files are copied and linked, which needs a compatible compiler on the node.
- `"copy"`: shared objects are copied, which needs a compatible node.
- `"auto"`, the default: `"copy"` when all nodes are `"localhost"`, else `"compile"`.

The build runs once per node before the first task; `job.R` points every model object of the
workspace at the one shared object (`modelname()`). On SLURM it runs once on the login node for all
array tasks. Output goes to `build.log`; a failed build stops the submission and shows the end of
the log. `libs` prepends library paths on the nodes for build and tasks, expanded remotely, so `~`
is the remote home.

The coverage job has no model files: no model object in `input`, no shared object in the working
directory.

## Job monitoring and recovery

| function | does |
|---|---|
| `check()` | counts done, running, failed; `TRUE` once none runs, warns on failures |
| `wait(interval = 10)` | polls until none runs, reports changes; `TRUE` if all done |
| `get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE)` | returns the results |
| `log(i, lines = 20)` | last output lines of task `i` |
| `purge(local = FALSE)` | deletes the job folders on the nodes, on `"localhost"` the local `<jobname>_folder/<k>`, with `local = TRUE` also local folder and registry entry |
| `terminate()` | stops the tasks |

A task is done when the result file exists, running while the worker runs (also while waiting),
failed when the worker ended without a result. `get()` copies remote results over ssh into the
local `<jobname>_folder/<k>`, with `all = TRUE` all files. It joins parlists with `c()` and data
frames, parameter frames included, with `rbind()`, which merges the two sides of a profile; other
results come as a list. Missing results are dropped with a warning. `get(combine = FALSE)` returns
one entry per task, named like `tasks`: `NULL` if not done, the `try-error` if failed.
`terminate()` ends the process group of every slot, on SLURM the job by `scancel`.

Output of the second task, then deletion:

```{r purge, eval = TRUE}
job$log(2)
job$purge(local = TRUE)
```

`distributedComputing(wait = TRUE)` waits, returns `get()` and deletes the job; a job with failed
tasks is kept for `log()`.

A job outlives the session. The manifest is in the local `<jobname>_folder`, in the
`<jobname>_folder` of every remote node until `purge()`, and in the registry
`tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "data")` until `purge(local = TRUE)`;
`dMod2Jobs()` lists registered jobs. `recover = TRUE` with a job name returns the job functions
without resubmitting, from the manifest in the working directory, else the registry, else, with
`on`, the remote node folders, which recovers a job from another machine. A new job of the same
name is an error while the old one runs where the new one would replace the old folders: in the same
working directory or on the same remote nodes, also from another machine.

```{r}
dMod2Jobs()
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", recover = TRUE)
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")),
                            recover = TRUE)
```

## SLURM clusters

`slurmCluster()` names the login node, reached by ssh, and the resources per array task: `cores`,
`walltime`, `memPerCore` in GB. Workers are the `array` array tasks, by default one per task;
array task `j` runs tasks `j`, `j + array`, `j + 2 * array`, ... in sequence. The stage goes to
`~/<jobname>_folder/1` on the login node, where the template environment is set up, the model
files are built once, and `sbatch` submits from that folder, so compute nodes must see the
login-node home directory. `partition`, `account`, `maxRunning` (array tasks at once) and `sbatch`
(further options such as `"--constraint=ib"`) override the `#SBATCH` lines of the template. The
start reports the job ID; `check()` reads `squeue`, `terminate()` calls `scancel`.

`slurmTemplate()` sets up the job script template once per login node, stored in
`tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "config")`. A template is a cluster job script with placeholders
`{{ jobname }}`, `{{ ntasks }}` (array tasks), `{{ cores }}`, `{{ memPerCore }}`,
`{{ walltime }}`, and one line `{{ run }}` that runs the tasks. Non-comment lines before
`{{ run }}` set up the environment, e.g. `module load`, also for the build on the login node. A
placeholder without value is an error, so `{{ walltime }}` needs `walltime`. The shipped template
for the bwForCluster Helix:

```{r template, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines(system.file("slurm", "helix.sh", package = "dMod2")))
```

```{r}
slurmTemplate("mycluster", from = "~/mycluster.sh")   # once, from a job script, for editing
slurmTemplate("helix")                                 # the template dMod2 ships for Helix
slurmTemplate()                                        # the templates set up
cluster <- slurmCluster("helix", cores = 1, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

`slurmCluster(jobscript = )` takes another template for one job.

## Fits and profiles of the guide project

A cluster starts many small tasks sooner than one large one, so these jobs use one core per task.
The 200 fits of `fit.R` ([Optimization](guide-optimization.html)) as 200 one-fit tasks, each start
drawn from the task seed:

```{r}
free <- setdiff(names(mu), names(gauge))
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 1, iterlim = 1000, tolControl = tolerances),
  tasks = 200, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
fitsJob$check()
fitsJob$wait(interval = 60)
fits <- as.parframe(fitsJob$get())
fitsJob$purge(local = TRUE)
```

The sources of `obj` compile once on the login node. `get()` joins the parlists, `as.parframe()`
sorts by value. A later session, also on another day, takes up the job by name:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(jobname = "oppelt_fits", recover = TRUE)
```

The profiles of [Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html), one side of one parameter per task:

```{r}
sides <- expand.grid(par = names(best), side = c("left", "right"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
profilesJob <- distributedComputing(
  profile(obj, best, task$par, side = task$side, fixed = gauge,
          limits = c(lower = -7, upper = 7), stepControl = list(stop = "data"),
          algoControl = list(reoptimize = TRUE),
          optControl = list(iterlim = 100, tolControl = tolerances)),
  tasks = sides, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_profiles",
  input = c("obj", "best", "gauge", "tolerances"))
profilesJob$wait(interval = 60)
profiles <- profilesJob$get()
```

`get()` binds both sides of each parameter into one profile.

An `msem()` multistart splits by `which`: every task draws all starts from the same seed and fits
those it names. The 200 starts of [Sparse deviations](guide-sparse-deviations.html), two per task:

```{r}
compoundsJob <- distributedComputing({
  set.seed(3)
  msem(objCompounds + priorCompounds, random, init, fixed = gaugeReduced, fits = 200,
       sd = sdStart, keepFits = TRUE, which = task)
}, tasks = split(1:200, rep(1:100, each = 2)), on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_compounds",
input = c("objCompounds", "priorCompounds", "random", "init", "gaugeReduced", "sdStart"))
fitCompounds <- compoundsJob$get()
```

`get()` returns one `msem()` fit, the best, with table and fits of all starts. `helix.R` of the
project runs the other expensive guide scripts the same way.

Without SLURM, as many tasks run at once as there are nodes. One task per node, the default, with
ten fits per node core:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 10 * cores, iterlim = 1000,
          tolControl = tolerances, cores = cores),
  on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")), jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
```

[Bile acid transport](bileAcidTransport.html) runs the multistarts as a local job,
[Kok 2020](kokMSB2020.html) the 200 fits as a SLURM array job.

## System requirements

- A POSIX shell locally (on Windows the `sh` of Rtools) and on every remote node, bash on remote
  nodes for `build = "compile"` (default) and `"link"`.
- Remote nodes: ssh with key authentication, dMod2 and cppDE for the R on the node `PATH` or in
  `libs`, a compiler for `build = "compile"`.
- SLURM: an account on the login node, a template from `slurmTemplate()`, a home directory visible
  to the compute nodes.
- `zstd` on every remote node if the local machine has it, since it then compresses the workspace.

Reference: `distributedComputing()`, `localNode()`, `sshNodes()`, `slurmCluster()`,
`slurmTemplate()`, `detectFreeCores()`, `dMod2Jobs()`, `mstrust()`, `msem()`, `profile()`
